A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

simple algorithms are better than complex ones for single-copy ortholog identification, and that paralogy is an important factor that must be considered in the design of ortholog identification algorithms.

the cRBH algorithm, with its simple and intuitive approach, is the best algorithm for the accurate identification of single-copy orthology in a model yeast clade.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ortholog prediction algorithms are highly sensitive to paralogs and that paralogs should be removed prior to ortholog prediction, especially in species that descended from whole genome duplication events.
the accuracy of ortholog prediction algorithms is highly sensitive to the taxon set used for algorithm parameter optimization and to the evolutionary history of the species under study.

the accuracy of an ortholog prediction algorithm depends on the specific evolutionary scenario being investigated, and that a careful evaluation of the algorithm is required before using it in an analysis.
